title: WPPIL/105/2013 of Sarita Sharma Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (PIL) No. 105 of 2013
Sarita Sharma. ........... Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. ............. Respondents
Mr. B.B. Sharma, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand / respondent Nos. 1
& 3.
Mr. Rahul Consul, Advocate for respondent No. 2.
Mr. Ramji Srivastava, Advocate for respondent No. 5.
JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.

Dated: 8th May, 2014
BARIN GHOSH, C. J.
Petitioner, an RTI Activist, Journalist and a Public Spirited Person,
seeks assistance of this Court for demolition of illegal construction of
Pacific Mall at Jakhan, Rajpur Road, Dehradun, and also demolition of
illegal construction of Hotel Moti Mahal, Gandhi Road, Dehradun.
According to the petitioner, Pacific Mall as well as Hotel Moti Mahal
have been constructed in excess of the sanctioned area in the map
sanctioned by Mussoorie Dehradun Development Authority, respondent
No. 2. The person responsible for construction of Pacific Mall is Saket
Bansal, respondent No. 5, and the person responsible for construction of
Hotel Moti Mahal is Vimal Singh, respondent No. 6. The other
respondents in the petition are the State of Uttarakhand; District
Magistrate, Dehradun; and Nagar Nigam, Dehradun. Notice was issued to
the respondents. All of them were served with the notice. Respondent
No. 5 entered appearance and contested the petition. Respondent No. 6,
despite being served, did not enter appearance, nor contested the petition.

2
2. Petitioner has annexed a positive print of a photograph of Pacific
Mall to the petition; wherefrom, it appears that the building of the Mall
stands completely constructed. No such photograph of Hotel Moti Mahal
has been annexed to the petition. In paragraph 6 of the petition, it has
been alleged that Pacific Mall is being constructed in contravention of the
provisions of the U.P. Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973
(hereinafter referred to as the "said Act"); in violation of the Government
Orders issued by the State of Uttarakhand from time to time; and without
obtaining permission of the official / statutory respondents to the petition.
It has been alleged that respondent No. 2 had issued a notice pertaining to
the said Mall for violation of the provisions of the said Act; but, still,
construction of the Mall is continuing and the official / statutory
respondents are not taking action against such construction. In
paragraph 7 of the petition, it has been alleged that, originally, sanction
was granted for a small building, but a multi-storeyed building is being
constructed in excess of the area shown in the map and against the
sanction. In paragraph 9 of the petition, it has been stated that
construction is being made on about 4000 sq. ft. of land belonging to
PWD / Nagar Nigam, Dehradun. It has been stated that the police has
been approached by the respondent No. 2 for stopping illegal
construction, but of no avail. In paragraph 10 of the petition, it has been
stated that unauthorised construction is being made on Khasra Nos. 52, 55
& 61 of Village Jakhan, Rajpur Road, Dehradun. To the petition, a Show-Cause Notice dated 22nd December, 2011; Order directing stoppage of
construction dated 22nd December, 2011; and a request made to the police
for stoppage of construction dated 22nd December, 2011, all issued by
respondent No. 2, were annexed. The said action was taken on the basis
of a complaint dated 17th December, 2011 made by one Junior Engineer,
which, too, was annexed. The petition, however, was filed on 19th
August, 2013 after making oral complaints, as stated in paragraph 13 of
the petition.
3. In paragraph 15 of the petition, it has been stated that large number
of residential, commercial buildings and hotels are being constructed at

3
Rajpur Road, Dehradun, since January, 2011 in contravention of the
provisions of the said Act; but no action is being taken against
unauthorised construction of Hotel Moti Mahal, Gandhi Road, Dehradun,
being made by respondent No. 6. There is no other assertion in relation to
construction of Hotel Moti Mahal in the petition.
4. A counter affidavit has been filed by one Manish Kumar Jain on
behalf of Pacific Development Corporation Ltd., where it has been stated
that the said Company is responsible for construction of the said Mall. In
that, it has been stated, amongst others, that the petitioner is neither a
public spirited person, nor is espousing any public cause; but is a part of a
gang of blackmailers and working in concert with Rahul Bhatia and
Virendra Singh Panwar.
5. In the said affidavit, on merits, it has been stated that, while making
the construction of the said Mall, no public land or Government land has
been encroached. It has been stated that the said Mall has been
constructed on a land measuring an area of 13,066 sq.mtrs. in Khasra Nos.
139, 140, 141 & 142 (Old Khasra Nos. 52, 55 & 61) situate at Village
Jakhan, Rajpur Road, Dehradun. It has been stated that the said Mall is
situate on the main Rajpur Road and the adjoining plots have already been
used for commercial purposes, as there are a number of shopping
complexes besides the said Mall. It has been stated that an application
was made to respondent No. 2 for development of the property belonging
to the said Company with requisite fees after obtaining all necessary
NOCs from different departments. In response thereto, respondent No. 2,
vide order No. C0431/2011, granted the sanction. While construction on
the basis of such sanction was being made, due to market dynamics,
architectural changes became necessary, which were permissible under
the law. Such changes were reported by the Junior Engineer of
respondent No. 2, whereupon, a notice dated 22nd December, 2011 was
issued by the said respondent. The said Company, accordingly, applied
for compounding of the deviations after submission of all NOCs, as were
required by the said respondent. The said Company was asked to deposit

4
compounding fee of ` 1,52,44,528/- and, upon payment thereof,
compounded map was sanctioned by the said respondent. On the basis of
the said compounded sanctioned map, the said Mall has been constructed.
It has been contended that the original sanction was for a Mall and the
latter sanction was also for construction of a Mall, along with Hotel and
Multiplex. With the said affidavit, original sanctioned Map as also the
compounded Map were annexed, wherefrom, it appears that original plot
area was 12,686.84 sq.mtrs., which stood increased to 13,066.84 sq.mtrs;
as a result, the area of construction stood altered. However, the number of
floors to be constructed remained the same. With the said affidavit,
Environmental Clearance, issued by the State Level Environment Impact
Assessment Authority, Uttarakhand, dated 4th August, 2013, was also
annexed.
6. To the said affidavit, a rejoinder affidavit was filed by the
petitioner. In that, petitioner repeated that she is a public spirit lady and is
working for the welfare of the State of Uttarakhand. The other allegations
pertaining to blackmailing, etc. were denied, though not specifically. In
that affidavit, it was contended that the Mall has been constructed in
contravention of the Map on the Government land. It was urged that, in
the interest of justice, it is necessary that a survey be conducted. It has
been contended that respondent No. 5 has not filed affidavit to save his
legal liability. It has been stated that compounding has been done against
the rules and laws.
7. One Banshidhar Tiwari, in his capacity as the Secretary of
respondent No. 2, has also filed an affidavit. In that, it has been
specifically stated that no construction is allowed without the sanctioned
map under the provisions of the Uttarakhand (U.P. Urban Planning and
Development Act, 1973) Amendment Act, 2009. It has been stated that a
Map dated 28th April, 2011 was sanctioned for construction of the subject
Mall. Later, certain deviations were detected. Therefore, show-cause
notice under Sections 27 & 28 of the said Act, dated 22nd December,
2011, was issued. On 16th January, 2013, the said deviations were

5
compounded and compounding plan dated 16th January, 2013 was
sanctioned. It was stated that the original Map was for construction of a
Multiplex-cum-Commercial Mall & Group Housing and the compounded
Map was also for that purpose. It was stated that the deviations were
within the compoundable limits and, as such, the same were compounded.
It has also been stated that compounding fee of ` 1,52,44,588/- has been
realised. It has been asserted that there is no prohibition for construction
of such a building in the area, where the same was permitted to be
constructed. It has been specifically denied that there is any contravention
of Sections 25, 26, 27, 28, 14 or 15 of the said Act. It has further been
contended that the petition appears to be a personal interest litigation filed
under the garb of Public Interest Litigation.
8. A rejoinder affidavit to the counter affidavit filed by respondent
No. 2 was filed by the petitioner, where it has been contended that
respondent No. 2 has no power to compound the case under the said Act.
9. Subsequent thereto, with the permission of the Court, Manish
Kumar Jain filed yet another affidavit, where it was contended that the
petitioner, along with Rahul Bhatia and Virendra Singh Panwar, has
constituted Bhrashtachar Virodhi Sangharsh Samiti in order to blackmail
innocent people, who are carrying on their business particularly in
Dehradun and at adjoining places for extraneous considerations and have
made their profession to file writ petitions for oblique motives. To
support the said contention, copy of a news item was annexed.
10. The Court called upon the petitioner to disclose herself. In order to
do so, petitioner filed an affidavit. Thereby, she annexed her Voter's
Identity Card and held out that she is a correspondent / journalist of the
fortnightly Hindi Newspaper "Uttaranchal Crime News" published from
Dehradun. A copy of the Identity Card issued by Uttaranchal Crime
News was also annexed to the said affidavit. In addition thereto,
petitioner indicated that she has passed Intermediate Examination and has
annexed copy of the certificate issued in relation thereto. She also

6
indicated that, under the Right to Information Act, she has sought many
informations and annexed copies of the informations received in
connection therewith. In addition thereto, she held out that the residents
of the Officers' Enclave made a complaint pertaining to disposal of
sewage water from the said Mall. It was also alleged that respondent
No. 5 is accused in the income tax related chara ghotala case. Petitioner
also stated that a crime case was registered at Police Station Rajpur
against S.K. Bansal and others for negligent death of a labour. She stated
that respondent No. 5 is pressurizing the petitioner to withdraw the writ
petition and, accordingly, she has filed a complaint with S.S.P., Dehradun.
She has stated that the expenses for filing the writ petition have been
collected from the members of the NGO "Alert Women Rights Protection
Society". It has also been stated that the petitioner has been issued a
Permanent Account Number by the Income Tax Department, a copy
whereof has also been annexed.
11. With the leave of the Court, Manish Kumar Jain filed yet another
affidavit and, thereby, dealt with the last mentioned affidavit of the
petitioner. There, it has been contended that the name of Uttaranchal
Crime News has not been recorded in the website of Registrar of
Newspapers of India and, in connection therewith, information received in
relation thereto from the website of Registrar of Newspapers of India has
been annexed. It has been contended that the RTI activities, as appear
from the annexures to the affidavit of the petitioner, are in relation to
informations available with the Haridwar Development Authority and the
same has nothing to do with Dehradun. It was denied that respondent
No. 5 is an accused in income tax related chara ghotala case. It was
stated that the complaint made to S.S.P., Dehradun, is a false and
fabricated complaint.
12. Subsequent thereto, with the leave of the Court, Manish Kumar Jain
filed yet another affidavit. In that, it was stated that, on 14th March, 1996,
Naman Buildcon Ltd. was incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956.
Subsequent thereto, name of Naman Buildcon Ltd. was changed to Pacific

7
Development Corporation Ltd. Sri Saket Bansal, respondent No. 5, is one
of the Directors of the said Company. A copy of the fresh certificate of
incorporation was annexed to the said affidavit. It was stated that the said
Company, as owner, is in possession of land measuring 13,067.45
sq.mtrs. in Khasra Nos. 139Ka, 139Kha, 139Da, 139Cha, 139Jha, 140,
141 & 142 (Old Khasra Nos. 52, 55 & 61) situate at Village Jakhan,
Rajpur Road, Dehradun. To support the said contention, copy of the
khatauni was annexed to the said affidavit. To the said affidavit,
Completion Certificate dated 7th August, 2013, issued by respondent
No. 2, was also annexed. A copy of the letter dated 19th November, 2013,
written by Upper Tehsildar, Sadar, Dehradun, to the District Magistrate,
Dehradun, suggesting that the said Company is in possession of 13,024
sq.mtrs. of land, was also annexed to the said affidavit. It was also
alleged that, despite best efforts made, the deponent could not find even a
single copy of the newspaper by the name Uttaranchal Crime News
anywhere in Dehradun.
13. The last-mentioned affidavit of Manish Kumar Jain was dealt with
by the petitioner by filing an affidavit; but there, she did not deal with the
affidavit filed by Manish Kumar Jain prior thereto. In that, it has been
stated that Manish Kumar Jain is not a party to the writ petition; he is a
resident of Meerut; and has no authority to file counter affidavit or
supplementary affidavit on behalf of respondent No. 5.
14. With the leave of the Court, Manish Kumar Jain filed yet another
affidavit enclosing therewith a certified true copy of the Resolution passed
by the said Company authorising Manish Kumar Jain to represent the said
Company in the present litigation.
15. The pleadings as above raise three questions, namely, whether the
petition is mala fide; whether any public land has been encroached; and
whether there is power to compound and, if so, whether compounding has
been done within the permissible limit?

8
16. From what has been stated above, it would be evident that there is
no evidence that the petitioner had approached any of the authorities to
remedy the alleged ills complained of in the petition, except alleged oral
complaints. The fact remains that the petition was filed on 19th August,
2013 after the completion certificate dated 7th August, 2013 was issued.
Petitioner knew that steps under various provisions of the said Act have
been taken by respondent No. 2 on 22nd December, 2011; but, despite
such action, the building has been completed. Accordingly, petitioner
must be aware that, despite such steps being taken, the construction is
continuing and she approached the Court with a photograph showing that
construction of the building of the Mall stands complete. Petitioner
claims to be a Reporter of a newspaper, which, according to the said
Company, is not in existence and this fact has not been denied in the
pleadings by the petitioner. Petitioner was aware that the building of the
Mall has been constructed ultimately on a larger plot of land and alleged
that, while doing so, the building encroached Government / Public Works
Department land; but, she made no effort to establish the same even prima
facie. According to the said Company, petitioner and two of her
associates, named above, are blackmailers; but the said Company, at the
same time, has not been able to establish the same by any evidence
whatsoever. While the petitioner has asked for survey to be conducted by
the Court to ascertain whether encroachment has been made over any land
belonging to the Government / Public Works Department; the said
Company prayed for an inquiry into the background of the petitioner and
her associates. We were pondering over the same; but, ultimately,
concluded that it is not such a case, where any such inquiry should be
made, inasmuch as, it now stands accepted that the original land area has
been increased. Accordingly, as it appears to us, petitioner took a chance
to the effect that the increased area does not belong to the said
Company and, accordingly, made assertions, which have been proved to
be incorrect by the said Company as well as by the Upper Tehsildar,
Sadar, Dehradun. At the same time, there is no prima facie evidence that
the petitioner or her associates made any attempt to blackmail either
respondent No. 5 or anyone else. The newspaper report relied by the said

9
Company suggests that the petitioner and her associates had assembled at
a place to ventilate their grievances. We, accordingly, conclude the first
issue by holding that the petitioner had taken a chance to establish that the
said building has been constructed on the Government / Public Works
Department land.
17. As aforesaid, despite getting several opportunities to file pleadings
and despite the petitioner having filed a number of pleadings, she did not
bring on record anything to suggest, even prima facie, that any part of the
land, upon which the Mall has been constructed, belongs to the
Government / Public Works Department of the Government. The fact
remains that the State Government is a party to the petition. It has not
supported the contention of the petitioner that any part of the land
belonging to the Government / Public Works Department has been
encroached upon. In one of the affidavits filed by the petitioner, an
insinuation was given that land belonging to the Nagar Nigam has been
encroached. Nagar Nigam is respondent No. 4. The said respondent did
not make any such assertion. Furthermore, respondent No. 2 has held out
that the original sanction as well as the latter sanction were granted in
accordance with law. The said Company has asserted that the said Mall
has been constructed on the land belonging to it and that is evidenced by
the Khatauni. Upper Tehsildar, Sadar, Dehradun, has reported to the
District Magistrate what was stated in the letter dated 19th November,
2013. The District Magistrate is also a party to the petition. He has not
stated that any land belonging to the Government has been encroached.
In those circumstances, it cannot be held that any land belonging to the
Government / Nagar Nigam / Public Works Department has been
encroached.
18. The last question is, whether it is permissible to compound. Power
to compound has been given by Section 32 of the said Act. Section 57 of
the said Act has granted bye-laws making power to, amongst others, lay
down the principles of compounding; in terms whereof, Mussoorie
Dehradun Development Authority (Compounding of Offences) Bye-

10
Laws, 1998 have been made. In terms of Section 14 of the said Act, every
development requires permission. According to Section 2(e) of the said
Act, "development" includes re-development. In the instant case, a
second permission was sought. While granting such permission, it was
necessary to make inquiry in relation to any matter specified in Clause (d)
of Sub-Section (2) of Section 9 of the said Act and also in relation to any
other matter. That encompasses all such powers to grant a fresh or new
permission. The conclusion, therefore, would be that respondent No. 2
had power to compound and also to grant a revised permission. Despite
both the Maps being available, no attempt was made to show that either
the first Map or the second Map is contrary to any provision of law or that
any such Map could not be sanctioned.
19. We, accordingly, close the matter and dismiss the writ petition.
(V.K. Bist, J.) (Barin Ghosh, C. J.)
G
